skill.displayName: Work Productivity Gog Google Workflow Helper

llm.summary: This is a documentation-only workflow helper with overly broad activation wording, but it does not contain code, credential handling, persistence, or hidden actions.

dimensions.detail: The skill recommends local-friendly outputs such as scripts, templates, checklists, and CPU-safe workflows, and does not request direct access to Gmail, Drive, calendars, local files, credentials, or network APIs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains Markdown/YAML instructions only; no installer, executable script, dependency file, or remote payload retrieval was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger terms and implicit-invocation metadata are broad, including generic Google Workspace and CLI terms, so users should expect possible over-activation in loosely related requests.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence mechanism, background worker, memory modification, privilege escalation, tool wrapping, or system configuration change was present in the inspected files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to help produce workflows, checklists, analysis, templates, and implementation support for Gog/Google Workspace-style productivity tasks; the artifacts match that advisory purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, consider narrowing or explicitly invoking this skill because its keywords include broad terms like Google, workspace, CLI, Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Contacts, and bug fix. The artifact itself is low risk, but broad implicit activation could make it appear during unrelated productivity tasks.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: Verified broad keywords, broad example triggers, and allow_implicit_invocation in the artifacts; this is a routing-quality and user-control concern, but the skill is advisory text only and does not grant or instruct sensitive tool authority.
[SQP-3] expected: Verified mixed English and Chinese text in the Chinese README and SKILL file; this is consistent with mirrored bilingual documentation and source-evidence titles, and does not create a security concern.
[AIG SARIF] expected: The static scan reported no T01-T09 results; local inspection also found no executable code, remote execution, credential handling, persistence, or tool hijacking instructions.
